delivery: Source changes and isolated tests only; installed editor and Android APK not replaced
findings: Video writes were disconnected after 250 ms; short stalls caused unnecessary reconnects.
Android switched permanently to JPEG for the current stream after any first H.264 exception.
Closing HttpExchange synchronously could block the shared capture thread behind a stalled writer.
Write timeout ownership checks were not atomic with connection replacement.
Non-200 video HTTP responses were all presented as pairing failures.
changes: Video/JPEG write timeout is 1.5 seconds and tied atomically to the current connection.
Socket close is detached from capture and JavaFX threads; obsolete writers cannot clear a new deadline.
Android uses bounded retries with backoff, retaining H.264 through transient failures.
Three consecutive failures without five seconds of decoded frames allow JPEG fallback; five failures end retries.
Explicit unsupported video responses allow immediate fallback; 401/403 alone request pairing again.
Status reports current stream codec and the host's stalled-video disconnect counter.

validation.android_sources: All Android Java sources compiled locally against android.jar with Java 8 target
validation.python_http_udp: 10 tests passed outside the network-isolated sandbox
validation.stream_lifecycle: Deterministic short-stall, blocked close, old-writer and new-owner checks passed in isolated JavaFX host

environment.transport: Loopback, real hidden Windows OpenGL engine, Media Foundation hardware H.264, headless JavaFX

limitations: No Android device or phone Wi-Fi reachability/display-FPS validation; actual initial connection failure is not conclusively diagnosed.
No firewall or security configuration was changed.
Numbers use the animated-color fixture, not a complex gameplay workload.
macOS actual hardware and audio streaming were not run.
